claims.text: Integrating in situ neutron or X-ray scattering with a calibrated predictive simulation framework will predict phonon lifetimes in equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi with less than 10% deviation from experiment.
Real-time scattering measurements directly capture phonon dispersion.
Real-time scattering measurements directly capture dynamic phonon-scattering events.
Static models only approximate phonon dispersion and dynamic scattering events.
The proposed samples are bulk, equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys.
Vacuum induction melting followed by homogenization will minimize texture effects in the samples.
The framework will use in situ scattering data to measure phonon dispersion curves and lifetimes during thermal cycling.
Real-time observation of phonon dynamics and scattering events will mediate calibration between experimental observations and simulation outputs.
Feedback from direct in situ measurements will enable recalibration of the simulation models.
Dynamic calibration will improve the representation of phonon-scattering mechanisms and lifetimes.
Dynamic calibration will reduce uncertainty associated with static approximations.
Reducing uncertainty in phonon-scattering and lifetime models will produce more precise predictions of low thermal conductivity.
The approach will maintain less than 10% deviation between predicted and measured phonon lifetimes across room temperature to 800°C.
Current static simulation methods without real-time experimental calibration typically have errors exceeding 10% when predicting phonon lifetimes.
The approach is applicable to bulk equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800°C.
The effectiveness of the approach may diminish outside the stated composition and temperature range.
A consistent phonon-lifetime discrepancy above 10% across the tested temperature range after calibration will falsify the hypothesis.
